nodes.label: EMS — Environmental Management System (project brief)
nodes.rationale: Built for DENR-PENRO Dinagat Islands to track fuel, electricity, water and paper consumption plus ESWM and GHG compliance. Around five to ten concurrent users and fewer than twenty in total, one office, no multi-branch support.

nodes.label: ISO 14001:2015 compliance
nodes.rationale: The environmental management standard the tracked data supports compliance with. It is the reason the six consumption and compliance areas are the scope.

nodes.label: Fully offline LAN deployment
nodes.rationale: No internet dependency, accessible only inside the office network. Implies adapter-node rather than adapter-auto, no CDN-hosted assets, fonts or scripts, and session-based auth with no OAuth. Roughly 60 percent of clients are on WiFi, so session handling, form submissions and loading states must fail gracefully and recover rather than assume a rock-solid link.

nodes.label: The six tracked areas
nodes.rationale: Fuel, electricity, water, paper, ESWM and GHG. Each becomes both a staff module and an admin submodule in the permission definitions, and each will eventually need its own report documents.

nodes.label: Fuel is the only area with an approval step
nodes.rationale: A staff member requests a withdrawal slip and GSU approves it, but the approval itself is physical — somebody signs the printed slip and afterwards it is marked approved in the system. So the system records an approval that already happened on paper; it is not where the approving takes place. Approvers may approve their own submissions, which matches actual agency practice and is deliberate, not an oversight.

nodes.label: One role per user, no per-user overrides
nodes.rationale: Roles today are Admin, GSU and per-section Encoder/Focal roles, with the exact section-to-role mapping still to be decided. The small scale is why several design decisions accept a small residual risk rather than build machinery against it.

edges.source_location: Deployment — session-based auth only, and session handling must survive WiFi drops
